Theorem
[$L^p$ uniqueness for $p>1$] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0183 1. ch12:12.26\group Heat Equation Uniqueness

Let $(M,g)$ be any complete noncompact manifold and $1<p<\infty $. If $u\geq 0$ is a heat subsolution, $\int _0^{T'}\int _Mu^p<\infty $ for every $T'<T$, and $\lim _{t\downarrow 0}\int _Mu(x,t)^p\, d\mu =0$, then $u=0$ on $M imes [0,T)$.

Proof

\sketch Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0184 Let $\varphi _r$ be supported in $B(O,2r)$, equal to one on $B(O,r)$, and $| abla \varphi _r|^2\leq 3r^{-2}$. Multiplying the subsolution inequality by $p\varphi _r^2u^{p-1}$ and integrating by parts and in time gives

\[ \int _M\varphi _r^2u(T')^p+ rac{2(p-1)}p\int _0^{T'}\! \int _M \varphi _r^2| abla u^{p/2}|^2 \leq rac{6p}{(p-1)r^2}\int _0^{T'}\! \int _Mu^p. \]

Letting $r o \infty $ makes the right side vanish and proves $u(T')=0$.

□
